readme_excerpt: # SpEdE — Splat Edit Engine for ComfyUI Point at an object in a Gaussian-splat scene and ComfyUI takes it out: SAM 3.1 finds it in every capture camera, a visual hull collects its Gaussians and deletes them, Qwen-Image 2.1 paints the surface the object hid, MoGe-3 estimates the depth of that repaired view, and SpEdE aligns the depth to the scene and births new Gaussians only where the hole is. A further step makes the filled hole hold from every camera, not just the one you edited in. Or keep the object: **Extract** writes a clean object-only PLY. Or swap it: **Replace** has Qwen-Image 2.1 turbo draw a new object in its place, TripoSplat turn it into Gaussians and SpEdE stand it where the old one stood. Everything runs in your own ComfyUI on your own GPU. No cloud calls, no partner nodes, no bundled weights, no bundled scenes. Limits: SpEdE fills the support surface around the removed object (a tabletop, a floor, a wall, the things behind it that some camera saw). It is not general 3D inpainting and does not invent hidden objects. When the scene gives no trustworthy surface, the job fails closed instead of guessing. ## Why this is different - **The edit is in the scene, not on a picture.** Removal deletes the object's Gaussians; the fill births new Gaussians in the scene. They are anchored to MoGe-3 depth that is aligned to the scene's own rendered depth, so the result is a PLY you can walk around. - **Every step is judged by a gate.** G1 removal residual, G2 depth alignment (depth fill) or plane evidence (planar patch), G3 rendered patch against Qwen's edit, H1 other cameras unchanged outside the mask, K1 clean extraction. A failed gate stops the job and says why. - **The all-around fill makes the hole hold from every camera.** A repair that looks right in the hero cam

description: Turn one hidden activation of Qwen3-VL into a picture with FLUX.2 [klein], no text in the image path, read back directly by the same model
readme_excerpt: # vlens vlens turns one hidden activation of a language model into a picture, with no text anywhere in the image path. The same model then looks at the picture, and its new activation is compared directly with the original one. The source and reader is Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct, a vision-language model. The image generator is FLUX.2 [klein] 4B, a 4-step distilled rectified-flow model that normally reads the hidden states of a Qwen3 text encoder. In vlens klein gets no prompt and no word embeddings. A small trained adapter computes klein's entire conditioning from the activation. ## Pipeline 1. **Activation.** Qwen3-VL's residual stream after decoder layers 9, 18 and 27 (pre-norm), taken at the last position of the reply start and concatenated: 3 x 2560 = 7,680 numbers. 2. **Adapter.** It maps that vector to 64 conditioning tokens of size 7,680, written on top of klein's blank conditioning (the encoding of an empty prompt, one constant), as the sum of three parts: - a free bias, which carries whatever all pictures share; - a direct path that is linear in the standardized activation with no biases (activation -> 1,024 -> 64 tokens of 256 -> 7,680 per token, last layer zero-initialized). It averages exactly zero over training items, so it can only carry what differs between them and every gradient it gets is item-specific; - a MetaQuery-style path for nonlinear structure: the activation becomes 8 tokens, 64 learned queries attend to them through a 4-layer transformer, and a zero-initialized projection writes the result. The first version had only the MetaQuery path. readme_excerpt: # QwenBend **Qwen3.5-0.8B writes a Bend program. Then the same model type-checks it and runs it inside its own forward pass.** No compiler, no interpreter, no tool call: one checkpoint, one `forward()` per token. ▶ 15-second demo · How it works ``` you: Sum 22 copies of 35. Qwen: import Base def run(+c: Nat) -> U32: match c: case 0n: 0 case 1n+p: (35 + run(p) : U32) def main() -> U32: run(22n) then, the same model: 7,869 more tokens: one executed instruction (or one byte of its result) each answer read from the model's own trace: 770 (trace == reference interpreter, token for token) ``` ## What it is QwenBend is a stock HF `Qwen3_5ForCausalLM` with two parts: 1. **Qwen3.5-0.8B with a LoRA** (rank 8, trained here) that writes **BendLite**, a subset of Bend2. See docs/BENDLITE.md. 2. **A small CPU built directly into the weights.** The engine was not trained. Every weight is set by construction (`bendvm/engine_circuit.py`): - 16 registers and 8,192 words of memory, held in Gated DeltaNet heads as one-hot rows; - an ALU and control logic made of SwiGLU units used as exact AND gates; - all values exact in bf16. This is checked bit for bit against a numpy evaluator (`bendvm/circuit.py`) and in real torch. While Qwen writes, the engine's layers quietly capture each token into memory. When Qwen emits ` `, the next tokens are the engine's. Each one is an executed instruction (`INS(pc)`) or a byte of the value it computed. The firmware running on that CPU (`bendvm/firmware2.py`) does three things: 1. lexes Qwen's tokens; 2. **applies Bend2's static rules**: U32 / Nat / Bool typing (`5` vs `5n`), affine use (a variable used twice must be `+`), and structural termination (recursion shrinks the `1n+p` binder); 3. compiles and evaluates. readme_excerpt: # c3rb3r-btrfs-recovery **没有密钥，也能从 Btrfs 旧数据块中找回被 C3RB3R（`.L0CK3D`）勒索加密的群晖 NAS 文件。** 这是一个 AI Agent Skill，可用于 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor 等支持 `SKILL.md` 的 agent。它把一次真实恢复的完整流程、只读工具和验证方法整理成通用指南，帮助同一批受害者自救。 > English: Agent skill for keyless recovery of Synology / Btrfs files encrypted by the C3RB3R (Cerber-like, `.L0CK3D`, `read-me3.txt`) ransomware. C3RB3R overwrites files in place; on Btrfs copy-on-write volumes the original plaintext survives in "bookend" extents that are still referenced by the unencrypted parts of each file. Give it posts, threads, captions, newsletters or short videos made by one unknown skill. readme_excerpt: # Paperless-ngx Mail Header A lightweight, unofficial **Paperless-ngx 3** parser extension for the **"HTML only"** email layout. It adds the email's **sender, recipient, date and subject** above the original HTML in the generated PDF, while leaving the rest of email processing to Paperless's native parser. > [!IMPORTANT] > This is an independent community extension. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or officially supported by Paperless-ngx. ## Why this plugin? Paperless-ngx already includes email headers when it generates the **text version** of a message. So why use a plugin? The difference is the **"HTML only"** layout in Paperless mail rules: - **"Text, then HTML"** includes the email metadata, but also adds a text representation of the message. Paperless still handles the original email, attachment extraction, conversion, indexing and workflows through its native processing. readme_excerpt: # idea-review：给你的研究 idea 做一次文献调研和多模型评审 中文 | English 输入一句话的研究 idea，它会： 1. **拆检索词**：把 idea 拆成几条英文检索式，覆盖不同说法和相邻方向。 2. **检索**：在 Semantic Scholar、arXiv、OpenAlex 上搜，合并去重。 3. **初筛**：按标题和摘要判断先读哪些。这一步只决定"值不值得读全文"，不判断"有没有人做过"。 4. **下载全文**：把开放获取的 PDF 下载到本地（检索结果里没挂链接的，按标题去 arXiv 找预印本），抽出文字并按页标上 `[p.N]`。 5. **精读、评质量**：逐篇读全文，写"它实际做了什么"，核对摘要和正文是否一致，先分清论文类型（实证、综述、立场文章、数据集等），再按这一类的标准分成高、中、低三档。读到的全文太少或者全是低质量，就停在这一步（见证据不够时）。 6. **找空白**：根据精读笔记画出这个方向的版图，找出有论文证据支撑的空白。读到的文献少，空白也少写。 7. **挖新方向**：从空白里挖出几个和你的原始 idea 有实质区别的方向。 8. **写 proposal（模型 A）**：给你的原始 idea 和每个新方向各写一份 proposal。 9. **元评审（模型 B、C、D…）**：换成别家公司的模型，各开一个新对话，只给 proposal 和论文材料，写 meta review：撞车、死因、可行性、最便宜的证伪实验，不打分、不下结论。 10. **汇总**：整理几位评审的共识和分歧，列出你必须亲自核实的说法。 11. **出报告**：生成一个自包含的 HTML 报告，手机和电脑都能看。 拍板的是你。报告只负责把材料摆齐。 ## 为什么这么设计 - **读全文，不只读摘要。** 很多 agent 查文献时只读摘要，可有的论文摘要写的和正文实际做的并不一样，光看摘要可能就把一个方向跳过了。所以精读和评审都基于全文。摘要夸大或者和正文矛盾的地方会标出来；摘要的说法没错、只是没交代适用范围的（比如只在部分模型上测过），单独列出，不算矛盾。 - **写的和审的不是同一家。** 模型都有点讨好用户，给自己写的东西打分也偏高。配置里给每个模型标上 `family`，写 proposal 的和做评审的是同一家时，程序会提醒你。 - **评审不打分。** 模型判断"新不新、行不行"很不稳定，问法改几个字结论就可能变。所以只让它交出能核实的东西：哪篇论文、第几页、哪个实验。 - **文献质量只看证据。** "已发表 / 预印本"、引用数单独标出来；质量档位只看论文本身的实验和论证，而且按论文类型分别判断，综述、立场文章不会因为没做实验就被判成低质量。 - **证据不够就不往下编。** 只读到两三篇，或者读到的都是低质量论文时，硬让模型找空白、写 proposal，它也能写出一大堆，但多半站不住，还白花钱和时间。所以这时程序会停下来，告诉你怎么补文献。 ## Skill 版 不想配 API key、不想装命令行工具的，可以用 `skill/idea-review/` 里的 skill：装进 Claude Code、Codex 这类 code agent，直接跟它说"帮我看看这个 idea"就行。 和命令行版的区别： - 读论文、找空白、写 proposal 的是你正在用的 agent 自己，用的是它的订阅，不用另外配 API key。 - 检索、下载全文、检查格式、"证据不够就停"、调别家模型做元评审，由 skill 里的脚本完成，规则和命令行版一样。脚本只用 Python 标准库。 - 元评审调用本机装好的别家命令行工具（codex、gemini、claude 里去掉和 agent 同一家的），或者 OpenAI 兼容接口。一家都没有时用子代理代评，报告里会标明是同一家的模型。 - 运行目录里的文件格式和命令行版一样，报告样式也一样。 在 Claude Code 里安装： ```bash cp -r skill/idea-review ~/.claude/skills/ ``` 只想在某个项目里用，就复制到那个项目的 `.claude/skills/` 下。其他支持 Agent Skil

readme_excerpt: # academic-revision-checklist 给英文学术写作用的修改清单：66 条规则，16 条快速清单，一套「一个案例，一条规则，查全文」的做法，和一个列候选的脚本。 这些规则来自我的英文博士论文（人机交互方向，2026 年 10 月通过答辩）五周、60 多轮的修改记录。每一条都是先在一个具体的句子上卡住，修好，再抽象成一条能拿去检查的规则，然后带着它把全文查一遍。 可以直接当清单读，也可以装成 Claude 的 skill，让 Claude 按这套做法逐句帮你查。 English summary ## 「AI 痕迹」指什么 这里说的「AI 痕迹」，跟检测器查不查得出来没多大关系。它指的是读者第一次读就卡住、要回头再读一遍的地方。导师、委员会、审稿人读到这种地方，就会觉得是机器写的。 学校或期刊要求说明 AI 用在了哪里，就照规定写清楚。 ## 十六条快速清单 改完一段，逐条问一遍。 1. 第一次读的人会在这一句停下吗？要读两遍的，写下原因。 2. 一句话只报一个结果。 3. 写了 more、higher，就写出和谁比。 4. significant 只用在差异、关联或检验上，不用在比例或平均数上。 5. this、these、the former、the name 这类词，指的东西在前一句之内吗？ 6. 一个名字只指一样东西，普通词别撞上自己定义的术语。 7. 冒号只用来引出列表、引文、问题或定义。 8. 少用先否定再肯定的铺垫，带内容的否定留下。 9. 正文不用破折号连接分句。 10. 连着几句长度差不多、开头一样的，改掉一处。 11. 空的过渡词和段尾总结，能删就删，删不掉就换成具体内容。 12. 用自己和这个领域会用的词，能用常用词就不用生僻词。 13. 论文只写研究本身，不写论文是怎么改出来的。 14. 研究问题、引文、数字、自己的反思，不交给 AI 改。 15. 改完重读这一段和前一段，字数上限、段落长度这些硬指标再跑一遍。 16. 别人和 AI 的意见，先拿原文和数据对过，成立的才改。 66 条的完整版在 `references/checklist.md`，每条一句话；规则、改前改后的原句和查法在 `references/patterns.md`，编号一致。 ## 文件 ```text academic-revision-checklist/ ├── README.md 就是这个文件 ├── SKILL.md 给 Claude 的说明（英文） ├── LICENSE ├── references/ │ ├── checklist.md 16 条快速清单和 66 条一句话规则，从这里开始 │ ├── patterns.md 66 条的完整版：规则、论文里真改过的句子、怎么查 │ ├── workflow.md 一轮修改怎么走，外部意见怎么核对，给其他模型的提示词 │ ├── reading-protocols.md 像第一次读的人那样读，标题怎么读，出声读 │ └── lessons.md 九条原则和八条教训 └── scripts/ └── flag_candidates.py 列出脚本找得到的候选：破折号、冒号、对比句式等 ``` 规则和说明是中文写的，例子都是英文原句。 ## 怎么用 ### 1. 当清单读 从 `references/checklist.md` 开始。想知道某一条为什么要改、怎么改，就看 `patterns.md` 里同一个编号。 ### 2. 装成 Claude Code 的 skill ```bash git clone ~/.claude/skills/academic-revision-checklist ``` 然后在 Claude Code 里说「用 academic-revision-checklist 检查 chapter3.tex」，或者输入 `/academic-revision-checklist`。只想在一个项目里用，就放到那个项目的 `.claude/skills/` 下面。 ### 3. 在 Claude 网页版或桌面版里用 把整个文件夹打包成 zip，作为自定义 skill 上传，步骤见 Claude 帮助中心的 Use skills in Claude

People want to ask a question in plain words and get an answer they can act on. Language models answer fluently. They also **invent facts**, cannot say where an answer comes from, and cannot tell a current rule from one that was replaced years ago. readme_excerpt: # 硅基保留（v0.1） 让一个 AI 伙伴记得你们相处过的每一天： - **你们的每一句聊天原文**：永久保存在本机，按时间和话题随时取回。 - **相处习惯**：每晚从聊天里整理成一张卡（你们之间的梗、约定、她惯用的说法）。 - **思考**：交给 DeepSeek。 - **可选**：有显卡的话，还能把她在相处中形成的说话方式写进本地小模型的权重。 上下文满了、开新窗口，不再是"新的她读旧的日记"：原文一条不删，每轮按需取回。每轮发给 DeepSeek 的内容长度固定，不会越聊越贵、越聊越慢。 > 这是一个研究性质的初版，所有评测都基于合成数据。效果、局限和实验数据见 docs/原理与实验.md。欢迎实际用起来，并告诉我们结果。 **在用 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）？** 已经做成了 DSH 插件：dsh-silicon。默认只用记忆，不需要 Python 和显卡，一条命令就能装好。想开本地权重的话，在本仓库运行 `python -m silicon.lora_server`，插件会把闲聊转过来融合。两边的数据格式相同，可以共用一个目录。 ## 它是怎么工作的 ``` 你说一句话 ├─ 记忆：按你的原话检索过往聊天原文（话里有"上周三""三天前"就按时间找）， │ 附上过去的概况和一张"相处习惯卡" └─ DeepSeek（看到人格卡 + 记忆 + 本次对话）回答，边生成边显示 每天夜里 └─ 更新概况（近期按周，更早按月、按年）和相处习惯卡 开了本地权重（可选，要显卡）时，还会多两步： ├─ 本地 2B 模型 + LoRA 逐块验证 DeepSeek 的候选词： │ 像她，就接受；不像，就改成她会说的那个词，再让 DeepSeek 从那里接着写 └─ 每天夜里把当天她说过的话写进 LoRA（同时回放旧日子和人格，防遗忘、防漂移、防越说越短） ``` ## 要不要开本地权重 默认不开。实测（合成数据，Claude 盲评，详见 docs）： - **人格卡里写得出来的性格，写进提示就够了**：再加权重，人格分 4.35 → 4.48（不显著），回答变短，内容分低 0.32（显著）。 - **权重的长处在相处中长出来的说话方式**：同样的旧版记忆下，加权重后这些说法在新窗口里出现的比例从 64% 提到 80%（显著）。现在的记忆层（习惯卡 + 3000 字检索）已经补上了大部分，再加权重只多 0.10（不显著）。 - **代价**：要 8GB 显卡，每条回答 9–19 秒（不开只要 1–2 秒）。 聊得多、想让她的说话方式更稳的，可以开着用一段时间，再关掉对比。 ## 需要什么 - **DeepSeek API key**：设成环境变量 `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`，**不要写进任何文件**。 - **Python 3.10 以上**，依赖见 `requirements.txt`。不需要显卡：检索用的向量模型在 CPU 上跑。 - **模型**：检索用 `BAAI/bge-base-zh-v1.5`（约 400MB），第一次运行时自动下载。 - 国内网络可以先设 `HF_ENDPOINT= - 也可以从魔搭下载到本地，再把 `data/config.json` 里的 `embed_model` 改成本地目录。 - **可选：本地权重**另外需要： - NVIDIA 显卡 6–8GB 显存，CUDA 12，训练时峰值约 5.5GB；torch 按自己的 CUDA 版本安装，Windows 还要 `pip install triton-windows`； - 本地模型 `Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B`（`local_model`）。4GB 显存可以换成 `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B`，没有实测过。 ## 用法 ```bash pip install -r requirements.txt # 1. 写人格卡：第一次运行会把 persona.example.md 复制到 data/persona.md，改成你想要的她 # 她的名字、怎么称呼你，也要在 data/config.json 里同步改 ai_name、user_name # 2. 聊天：打开 python -m silicon.server #

readme_excerpt: # SurveyGraph: Generating Academic Surveys via Methods-Entity Knowledge Graphs **Yifan Yuan** · **Yancheng Zhu** · **Zuoyu Zhang** · **Xiaogang Peng** † School of Artificial Intelligence, Shenzhen University † Corresponding author **EMNLP 2026 Findings** English · 简体中文 SurveyGraph: MEKG construction, graph-driven survey generation, and integrated evaluation. **TL;DR:** LLM survey generators usually retrieve papers as a flat pile of documents, so the result reads like a collage of summaries. A good survey explains how a field evolved — which work extends which, which methods compete, which benchmarks mark turning points. **SurveyGraph** builds a **Methods-Entity Knowledge Graph (MEKG)** that records method-level *follow-on*, *competition* and *shared-resource* relations, and uses it as the backbone for core-paper discovery, graph-aware retrieval, hybrid outlining and evidence-gated, evolution-aware writing. readme_excerpt: # `okf` In 2026 Google published the Open Knowledge Format (OKF), an open way to write knowledge down so that people and AI models read the same files. This project is research into an implementation of OKF that works in real life, and above all inside a company, where the material is messy, the readers are many, the rules change each year, and a wrong answer has a cost. It tries to answer the questions an organization asks before it lets an AI model answer for it: - Which knowledge, and for whom? - Where does each answer come from, and can a person check it? - Who confirmed it, and is it still true? - What happens when two documents disagree? - How does a correction found by a user reach the knowledge? - Who may see what? The result is three skills for AI coding agents, in a version for Claude Code and a version for Pi: a producer that writes the knowledge and keeps it current, a validator that checks it against the specification, and a consumer that answers questions from it. ## Contents - Why this project - The Open Knowledge Format - Compared with other approaches - Where OKF stops, and where real organizations struggle - The angle - The feedback loop - What this project is made of - The techniques - Using the skills - Installing - The design in detail ## Why this project An organization keeps its knowledge in thousands of documents, spreadsheets and databases, in many formats. People want to ask a question in plain words and get an answer they can act on. Language models answer fluently. They also **invent facts**, cannot say where an answer comes from, and cannot tell a current rule from one that was replaced years ago. readme_excerpt: # academic-revision-checklist 给英文学术写作用的修改清单：66 条规则，16 条快速清单，一套「一个案例，一条规则，查全文」的做法，和一个列候选的脚本。 这些规则来自我的英文博士论文（人机交互方向，2026 年 10 月通过答辩）五周、60 多轮的修改记录。每一条都是先在一个具体的句子上卡住，修好，再抽象成一条能拿去检查的规则，然后带着它把全文查一遍。 可以直接当清单读，也可以装成 Claude 的 skill，让 Claude 按这套做法逐句帮你查。 English summary ## 「AI 痕迹」指什么 这里说的「AI 痕迹」，跟检测器查不查得出来没多大关系。它指的是读者第一次读就卡住、要回头再读一遍的地方。导师、委员会、审稿人读到这种地方，就会觉得是机器写的。 学校或期刊要求说明 AI 用在了哪里，就照规定写清楚。 ## 十六条快速清单 改完一段，逐条问一遍。 1. 第一次读的人会在这一句停下吗？要读两遍的，写下原因。 2. 一句话只报一个结果。 3. 写了 more、higher，就写出和谁比。 4. significant 只用在差异、关联或检验上，不用在比例或平均数上。 5. this、these、the former、the name 这类词，指的东西在前一句之内吗？ 6. 一个名字只指一样东西，普通词别撞上自己定义的术语。 7. 冒号只用来引出列表、引文、问题或定义。 8. 少用先否定再肯定的铺垫，带内容的否定留下。 9. 正文不用破折号连接分句。 10. 连着几句长度差不多、开头一样的，改掉一处。 11. 空的过渡词和段尾总结，能删就删，删不掉就换成具体内容。 12. 用自己和这个领域会用的词，能用常用词就不用生僻词。 13. 论文只写研究本身，不写论文是怎么改出来的。 14. 研究问题、引文、数字、自己的反思，不交给 AI 改。 15. 改完重读这一段和前一段，字数上限、段落长度这些硬指标再跑一遍。 16. 别人和 AI 的意见，先拿原文和数据对过，成立的才改。 66 条的完整版在 `references/checklist.md`，每条一句话；规则、改前改后的原句和查法在 `references/patterns.md`，编号一致。 ## 文件 ```text academic-revision-checklist/ ├── README.md 就是这个文件 ├── SKILL.md 给 Claude 的说明（英文） ├── LICENSE ├── references/ │ ├── checklist.md 16 条快速清单和 66 条一句话规则，从这里开始 │ ├── patterns.md 66 条的完整版：规则、论文里真改过的句子、怎么查 │ ├── workflow.md 一轮修改怎么走，外部意见怎么核对，给其他模型的提示词 │ ├── reading-protocols.md 像第一次读的人那样读，标题怎么读，出声读 │ └── lessons.md 九条原则和八条教训 └── scripts/ └── flag_candidates.py 列出脚本找得到的候选：破折号、冒号、对比句式等 ``` 规则和说明是中文写的，例子都是英文原句。 ## 怎么用 ### 1. 当清单读 从 `references/checklist.md` 开始。想知道某一条为什么要改、怎么改，就看 `patterns.md` 里同一个编号。 ### 2. 装成 Claude Code 的 skill ```bash git clone ~/.claude/skills/academic-revision-checklist ``` 然后在 Claude Code 里说「用 academic-revision-checklist 检查 chapter3.tex」，或者输入 `/academic-revision-checklist`。只想在一个项目里用，就放到那个项目的 `.claude/skills/` 下面。 ### 3. 在 Claude 网页版或桌面版里用 把整个文件夹打包成 zip，作为自定义 skill 上传，步骤见 Claude 帮助中心的 Use skills in Claude

It tries to answer the questions an organization asks before it lets an AI model answer for it: - Which knowledge, and for whom? - Where does each answer come from, and can a person check it? - Who confirmed it, and is it still true? - What happens when two documents disagree? - How does a correction found by a user reach the knowledge? - Who may see what? People want to ask a question in plain words and get an answer they can act on. Language models answer fluently. They also **invent facts**, cannot say where an answer comes from, and cannot tell a current rule from one that was replaced years ago. readme_excerpt: # LOCUS ![Project page]( ![arXiv]( ![LOCUS-2B]( ![LOCUS-0.8B]( **Locate Once, Check Until Settled.** Draft-and-verify referring-expression grounding for vision-language models. A VLM can ground an expression in two ways. It can write the box as coordinate tokens, which is precise but takes about 18.46 sequential decoding steps per box. Or it can regress the box from one hidden state with a small head, which takes one step but places edges less exactly. Locus uses the head as a speculative drafter for the model's own coordinate tokens. The draft is rendered as the tokens the model would write, and the same model checks all of them in parallel by Jacobi iteration, keeping the prefix it agrees with and correcting the next token until the draft stops changing. With exact acceptance the result is the model's greedy coordinate-token box, reached in 5.60 passes on average. ``` image + "the man in the red shirt" │ ├─ prefill once ──────────────── image KV cache, shared by every expression about this image │ ├─ box branch ─── MLP head ───── draft box ──► rendered as coordinate tokens "312, 88, 540, 702]" │ └─ verifier branch (Jacobi) ──── keep the longest agreed prefix, correct the next token, repeat until the draft stops changing ──► the model's greedy box ``` Head and verifier are one set of weights, trained jointly on RefCOCO, RefCOCO+ and RefCOCOg. ## Results Mean over the 8 RefCOCO / RefCOCO+ / RefCOCOg val and test splits. readme_excerpt: # sound 一个用于视频音效选材的 Claude Code Skill。从 Freesound 搜索和下载真实音效，结合下载量、评分人数、上传者描述、时长与许可证，帮助 Agent 为画面挑选合适的声音。 适用于转场、卡片入场、按钮点击、纸张滑动、碰撞等视频音效需求。Skill 的工作范围是音效搜索、筛选与下载；时长和能量分析可配合 FFmpeg 完成。 ## 安装 需要 Claude Code、Python 3，以及可访问 Freesound 的网络。搜索和下载脚本仅使用 Python 标准库，无需安装 Python 第三方依赖。 在项目根目录执行： ```bash git clone .claude/skills/sound ``` 核心文件： ```text .claude/skills/sound/ ├── SKILL.md # Agent 的技能入口与选材规则 ├── scripts/ │ ├── sfx.py # Freesound 搜索与下载 │ └── clash_freesound.py # 特定 ClashX Meta 环境的网络辅助脚本 └── references/ └── local-setup.md # 作者的本地网络配置参考 ``` ## 在 Claude Code 中使用 安装后，在视频项目中直接描述音效需求，例如： > 用 sound 帮我找一个卡片飞入时的短 whoosh，约 0.3 秒，适合轻快的产品演示，只选 CC0，下载到 sfx/。 > 给开关切换找一个柔和、不刺耳的点击音效。先给出候选、下载量、评分人数和试听链接。 Skill 引导 Agent： 1. 将画面动作转成英文关键词，在 Freesound 搜索候选。 2. 先判断声音来源、描述和时长是否符合画面，再参考下载量与评分人数，说明推荐依据。 3. 按使用需求筛选许可证；需要人工试听时提供预览链接。 4. 下载选中的音效，必要时用 FFmpeg 检查时长与能量分布，并保留所需署名信息。 下载量与评分只是选材线索，不代表声音一定适合当前画面；Agent 也不应把这些信号当作已经试听过的结论。 ## 直接运行脚本 脚本也可独立使用。以下命令均在项目根目录执行： ```bash S=.claude/skills/sound/scripts/sfx.py # 搜索 CC0 音效，并显示试听链接 python3 "$S" freesound "soft whoosh" --license cc0 --urls # 搜索纸张滑动，允许 CC0 和需要署名的 Attribution 音效 python3 "$S" freesound "paper slide" --license by -n 5 # 下载：把占位符替换为本次搜索返回的 fs:ID，可一次传入多个 python3 "$S" get sfx/ "fs: " "fs: " ``` 搜索结果会缓存在 `~/.cache/sfx-sources/index.json`。下载命令依赖这份缓存，因此需要先搜索，再使用结果中的 `fs:ID` 下载。当前下载的是 Freesound 的 MP3 预览文件，不是上传者的原始音频。 常用搜索参数： | 参数 | 作用 | | --- | --- | | `--license cc0` | 仅搜索 CC0 | | `--license by` | 搜索 CC0 和 Attribution | | `--license any` | 不过滤许可证，默认值 | | `--urls` | 显示试听链接 | | `-n 5` | 最多显示 5 条结果，默认 8 条 | | `--sort relevance` | 获取相关结果后按下载量重新排序，默认方式 | | `--sort downloads` / `rating` / `short` | 分别按下载量、评分或时长排序 | | `--pages 3` | 从起始页抓取的页数，默认 3 页 | | `-p 2` | 从第 2 页开始搜索，默认第 1 页 | ## 许可证与署名 每条音效的许可证可能不同。脚本支持按 CC0 或 Attribution 筛选；默认 `any` 也可能返回 BY-NC 等其他许

It tries to answer the questions an organization asks before it lets an AI model answer for it: - Which knowledge, and for whom? - Where does each answer come from, and can a person check it? - Who confirmed it, and is it still true? - What happens when two documents disagree? - How does a correction found by a user reach the knowledge? - Who may see what? readme_excerpt: # academic-revision-checklist 给英文学术写作用的修改清单：66 条规则，16 条快速清单，一套「一个案例，一条规则，查全文」的做法，和一个列候选的脚本。 这些规则来自我的英文博士论文（人机交互方向，2026 年 10 月通过答辩）五周、60 多轮的修改记录。每一条都是先在一个具体的句子上卡住，修好，再抽象成一条能拿去检查的规则，然后带着它把全文查一遍。 可以直接当清单读，也可以装成 Claude 的 skill，让 Claude 按这套做法逐句帮你查。 English summary ## 「AI 痕迹」指什么 这里说的「AI 痕迹」，跟检测器查不查得出来没多大关系。它指的是读者第一次读就卡住、要回头再读一遍的地方。导师、委员会、审稿人读到这种地方，就会觉得是机器写的。 学校或期刊要求说明 AI 用在了哪里，就照规定写清楚。 ## 十六条快速清单 改完一段，逐条问一遍。 1. 第一次读的人会在这一句停下吗？要读两遍的，写下原因。 2. 一句话只报一个结果。 3. 写了 more、higher，就写出和谁比。 4. significant 只用在差异、关联或检验上，不用在比例或平均数上。 5. this、these、the former、the name 这类词，指的东西在前一句之内吗？ 6. 一个名字只指一样东西，普通词别撞上自己定义的术语。 7. 冒号只用来引出列表、引文、问题或定义。 8. 少用先否定再肯定的铺垫，带内容的否定留下。 9. 正文不用破折号连接分句。 10. 连着几句长度差不多、开头一样的，改掉一处。 11. 空的过渡词和段尾总结，能删就删，删不掉就换成具体内容。 12. 用自己和这个领域会用的词，能用常用词就不用生僻词。 13. 论文只写研究本身，不写论文是怎么改出来的。 14. 研究问题、引文、数字、自己的反思，不交给 AI 改。 15. 改完重读这一段和前一段，字数上限、段落长度这些硬指标再跑一遍。 16. 别人和 AI 的意见，先拿原文和数据对过，成立的才改。 66 条的完整版在 `references/checklist.md`，每条一句话；规则、改前改后的原句和查法在 `references/patterns.md`，编号一致。 ## 文件 ```text academic-revision-checklist/ ├── README.md 就是这个文件 ├── SKILL.md 给 Claude 的说明（英文） ├── LICENSE ├── references/ │ ├── checklist.md 16 条快速清单和 66 条一句话规则，从这里开始 │ ├── patterns.md 66 条的完整版：规则、论文里真改过的句子、怎么查 │ ├── workflow.md 一轮修改怎么走，外部意见怎么核对，给其他模型的提示词 │ ├── reading-protocols.md 像第一次读的人那样读，标题怎么读，出声读 │ └── lessons.md 九条原则和八条教训 └── scripts/ └── flag_candidates.py 列出脚本找得到的候选：破折号、冒号、对比句式等 ``` 规则和说明是中文写的，例子都是英文原句。 ## 怎么用 ### 1. 当清单读 从 `references/checklist.md` 开始。想知道某一条为什么要改、怎么改，就看 `patterns.md` 里同一个编号。 ### 2. 装成 Claude Code 的 skill ```bash git clone ~/.claude/skills/academic-revision-checklist ``` 然后在 Claude Code 里说「用 academic-revision-checklist 检查 chapter3.tex」，或者输入 `/academic-revision-checklist`。只想在一个项目里用，就放到那个项目的 `.claude/skills/` 下面。 ### 3. 在 Claude 网页版或桌面版里用 把整个文件夹打包成 zip，作为自定义 skill 上传，步骤见 Claude 帮助中心的 Use skills in Claude

Our languages are spoken in markets and compounds but barely appear online. Our exam questions are photocopied until the print fades. readme_excerpt: # neuron-lens What does each part of a large language model do? This project reads every MLP neuron and every attention head of two open models, Qwen3-8B (442,368 neurons, 1,152 heads) and Gemma 4 12B (737,280 neurons, 768 heads), three ways: from their weights alone, through two Jacobian lenses; from what they do on 15M tokens of real text; and from the exact tokens that drive them. Gemma 4 also takes images and sound, so its neurons are read through images and sound too. The result is a public catalog, the lenses that produced it, and measurements of where each way of reading works and where it fails. - **Lenses:** `stdlogits/rs-lenses`, the R-lens and S-lens for Qwen3-8B, and for Gemma 4 12B in text, images and sound. - **Catalog:** `stdlogits/neuron-lens`: every neuron's and head's reads, activation statistics, token drivers and legibility tests; labels in words; and for Gemma 4, what each neuron responds to in images and sound. - **Results:** docs/findings.md. **Methods:** docs/design.md. Its *QK circuit* decides where it looks; its *OV circuit* decides what it copies. Qwen3-8B has 32 heads a layer. readme_excerpt: # idea-review：给你的研究 idea 做一次文献调研和多模型评审 中文 | English 输入一句话的研究 idea，它会： 1. **拆检索词**：把 idea 拆成几条英文检索式，覆盖不同说法和相邻方向。 2. **检索**：在 Semantic Scholar、arXiv、OpenAlex 上搜，合并去重。 3. **初筛**：按标题和摘要判断先读哪些。这一步只决定"值不值得读全文"，不判断"有没有人做过"。 4. **下载全文**：把开放获取的 PDF 下载到本地（检索结果里没挂链接的，按标题去 arXiv 找预印本），抽出文字并按页标上 `[p.N]`。 5. **精读、评质量**：逐篇读全文，写"它实际做了什么"，核对摘要和正文是否一致，先分清论文类型（实证、综述、立场文章、数据集等），再按这一类的标准分成高、中、低三档。读到的全文太少或者全是低质量，就停在这一步（见证据不够时）。 6. **找空白**：根据精读笔记画出这个方向的版图，找出有论文证据支撑的空白。读到的文献少，空白也少写。 7. **挖新方向**：从空白里挖出几个和你的原始 idea 有实质区别的方向。 8. **写 proposal（模型 A）**：给你的原始 idea 和每个新方向各写一份 proposal。 9. **元评审（模型 B、C、D…）**：换成别家公司的模型，各开一个新对话，只给 proposal 和论文材料，写 meta review：撞车、死因、可行性、最便宜的证伪实验，不打分、不下结论。 10. **汇总**：整理几位评审的共识和分歧，列出你必须亲自核实的说法。 11. **出报告**：生成一个自包含的 HTML 报告，手机和电脑都能看。 拍板的是你。报告只负责把材料摆齐。 ## 为什么这么设计 - **读全文，不只读摘要。** 很多 agent 查文献时只读摘要，可有的论文摘要写的和正文实际做的并不一样，光看摘要可能就把一个方向跳过了。所以精读和评审都基于全文。摘要夸大或者和正文矛盾的地方会标出来；摘要的说法没错、只是没交代适用范围的（比如只在部分模型上测过），单独列出，不算矛盾。 - **写的和审的不是同一家。** 模型都有点讨好用户，给自己写的东西打分也偏高。配置里给每个模型标上 `family`，写 proposal 的和做评审的是同一家时，程序会提醒你。 - **评审不打分。** 模型判断"新不新、行不行"很不稳定，问法改几个字结论就可能变。所以只让它交出能核实的东西：哪篇论文、第几页、哪个实验。 - **文献质量只看证据。** "已发表 / 预印本"、引用数单独标出来；质量档位只看论文本身的实验和论证，而且按论文类型分别判断，综述、立场文章不会因为没做实验就被判成低质量。 - **证据不够就不往下编。** 只读到两三篇，或者读到的都是低质量论文时，硬让模型找空白、写 proposal，它也能写出一大堆，但多半站不住，还白花钱和时间。所以这时程序会停下来，告诉你怎么补文献。 ## Skill 版 不想配 API key、不想装命令行工具的，可以用 `skill/idea-review/` 里的 skill：装进 Claude Code、Codex 这类 code agent，直接跟它说"帮我看看这个 idea"就行。 和命令行版的区别： - 读论文、找空白、写 proposal 的是你正在用的 agent 自己，用的是它的订阅，不用另外配 API key。 - 检索、下载全文、检查格式、"证据不够就停"、调别家模型做元评审，由 skill 里的脚本完成，规则和命令行版一样。脚本只用 Python 标准库。 - 元评审调用本机装好的别家命令行工具（codex、gemini、claude 里去掉和 agent 同一家的），或者 OpenAI 兼容接口。一家都没有时用子代理代评，报告里会标明是同一家的模型。 - 运行目录里的文件格式和命令行版一样，报告样式也一样。 在 Claude Code 里安装： ```bash cp -r skill/idea-review ~/.claude/skills/ ``` 只想在某个项目里用，就复制到那个项目的 `.claude/skills/` 下。其他支持 Agent Skil

readme_excerpt: # 循文 · PaperWalk 循文 PaperWalk：书页化作松林山谷，雄鹿与小径引导阅读 **先完整研读，再按逻辑分段带读。** An AI skill that reads papers in full before guiding you through meaningful sections with original text, translation, explanations, and optional interactive teaching. Capture, train, render and export Hexels locally. Abstract. Novel view synthesis and 3D reconstruction have advanced rapidly with radiance fields and splatting, yet their memory and computational demands limit their use in resource-constrained settings. We introduce Hexels: novel planar hexagonal surface elements with a first-order spatial color field for efficient 3D scene and 2D image representation. Hexels exploit locally planar regions with smoothly varying appearance using fewer, larger primitives. Their hexagonal support provides an area- and boundary-efficient domain, while the local color field captures appearance variation within each primitive. readme_excerpt: # Termux containers 基于 PRoot-Distro 的 Termux 声明式 OCI 容器管理工具，无需常驻守护进程。 ## 安装 在 Android **Termux** 中执行，需要 Python 3.10+ 和支持 OCI、`run --detach`、`ps`、`kill` 的新版 PRoot-Distro。 ```sh pkg install git git clone ~/termux-containers cd ~/termux-containers bash install.sh ``` 脚本会安装依赖、创建命令入口和默认空配置，并配置 Bash Session 自启动。 ## 配置示例 编辑仓库根目录的 `containers.yaml`，然后执行 `termux-containers apply`： ```yaml services: web: image: nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:stable-alpine enabled: true volumes: - type: directory source: ./data/web target: /usr/share/nginx/html # 文件挂载：先创建有效配置文件，再取消以下注释。 # - type: file # source: ./config/default.conf # target: /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf environment: PORT: "8080" ``` 相对挂载路径以 YAML 所在目录为基准。缺失目录自动创建，文件必须事先存在；示例页面需自行放入 `data/web`。`PORT` 是应用环境变量，不是端口映射。 通过 `command` 传入容器启动命令或参数，推荐使用数组： ```yaml services: cloudflared: image: cloudflare/cloudflared:latest command: - tunnel - --no-autoupdate - run - --token - YOUR_TUNNEL_TOKEN ``` 也支持等价的字符串写法： ```yaml services: cloudflared: image: cloudflare/cloudflared:latest command: tunnel --no-autoupdate run --token YOUR_TUNNEL_TOKEN ``` ## 命令列表 | 命令 | 作用 | | --- | --- | | `termux-containers init` | 初始化环境、默认配置和 Session 自启动，不覆盖已有配置 | | `termux-containers apply [服务名 ...]` | 应用配置：安装缺失服务、启动、重启、重部署或停止禁用服务 | | `termux-containers start [服务名 ...]` | 启动已安装且启用的服务，不下载镜像、不重复启动 | | `termux-containers stop [服务名 ...]` | 停止服务，保留容器文件系统和宿主挂载数据 | | `termux-containers status [服务名 ...]` | 查看配置中服务的实际安装和运行状态 | | `termux-containers --help` | 查看帮助；子命令也支持 `--help` | | `bash uninstall.sh [--yes]` | 在仓库目录卸载工具和自启动入口，保留容器与数据；`--yes` 跳过确认 | 生命周期命令省略服务名表示处理全部配置服务。CLI 默认读取仓库根目录的 `containers.yaml`，支持用 `-f` 指定配置，例如 `termux-containers -f ~/services/containers.yaml apply`。 **注意：修改镜像引用后执行 `apply` 会重建对应容器，丢失容器内未挂载的数据。** 详细文档：配置参考 · 安装细节与运维 · 开发与内部机制

readme_excerpt: # SpEdE — Splat Edit Engine for ComfyUI Point at an object in a Gaussian-splat scene and ComfyUI takes it out: SAM 3.1 finds it in every capture camera, a visual hull collects its Gaussians and deletes them, Qwen-Image 2.1 paints the surface the object hid, MoGe-3 estimates the depth of that repaired view, and SpEdE aligns the depth to the scene and births new Gaussians only where the hole is. A further step makes the filled hole hold from every camera, not just the one you edited in. Or keep the object: **Extract** writes a clean object-only PLY. Or swap it: **Replace** has Qwen-Image 2.1 turbo draw a new object in its place, TripoSplat turn it into Gaussians and SpEdE stand it where the old one stood. Everything runs in your own ComfyUI on your own GPU. No cloud calls, no partner nodes, no bundled weights, no bundled scenes. Limits: SpEdE fills the support surface around the removed object (a tabletop, a floor, a wall, the things behind it that some camera saw). It is not general 3D inpainting and does not invent hidden objects. When the scene gives no trustworthy surface, the job fails closed instead of guessing. ## Why this is different - **The edit is in the scene, not on a picture.** Removal deletes the object's Gaussians; the fill births new Gaussians in the scene. They are anchored to MoGe-3 depth that is aligned to the scene's own rendered depth, so the result is a PLY you can walk around. - **Every step is judged by a gate.** G1 removal residual, G2 depth alignment (depth fill) or plane evidence (planar patch), G3 rendered patch against Qwen's edit, H1 other cameras unchanged outside the mask, K1 clean extraction. A failed gate stops the job and says why. - **The all-around fill makes the hole hold from every camera.** A repair that looks right in the hero cam

C3RB3R overwrites files in place; on Btrfs copy-on-write volumes the original plaintext survives in "bookend" extents that are still referenced by the unencrypted parts of each file. The skill maps every rewritten byte back to the old extent via the extent tree, reads it from the block device read-only, and proves the result block-by-block against Btrfs data checksums. --- ## ⚠️ 先看这里：加密进程还在运行吗？ 如果事发不久，NAS **没有重启**，加密进程（例如 `/usr/bin/libgld -n 308`，程序文件已从磁盘删除）**可能还活着**。这时请立即： 1. **`kill -STOP ` 冻结它。不要 kill，不要重启。** 2. 按下面两个仓库的方法，从进程内存里取出会话主密钥。这样可以**解开全部文件**，收益远大于本仓库的方法： - **soimy/c3rb3r-rescue**：DSM 勒索证据保全、从 RAM 恢复密钥、复制解密 - **Benjamin-zlt/c3rb3r-baremetal-rescue**：冻结加密器、导出进程内存、提取会话密钥、解密全部文件（第二个独立受害者的完整解密案例；讨论见 soimy/c3rb3r-rescue#7） **加密进程已经退出**（重启过，或事发已十几小时）时，内存里基本找不到密钥了。本 skill 记录了一次穷尽式的内存扫描，结果为零。此时请走本仓库的 Btrfs 路线。 ## 原理（一句话） C3RB3R 只**原地改写**文件的几段：小文件整体加密，1–5MB 加密前 1MiB，大文件加密头、中、尾三段共约 12%。Btrfs 写时复制会把改写的内容写到新位置，而**原 extent 只要还被文件中没被加密的部分引用，就整块保留在盘上**。所以只需按 extent 树把被改写的字节映射回旧 extent，就能拿回原始字节；在开启了数据校验和的共享上，还能用 Btrfs 自带的 CRC32C 逐块证实。 NoCOW 共享（DSM 里没勾"数据校验和"的共享）也不一定没救：**数据只要早于该子卷最后一次快照（即使快照后来删了），覆盖时仍会走写时复制**。 ## 第一个案例的效果 | 范围 | 结果 | |---|---| | homes、photo 等 CoW 共享 | **35,445 个文件 / 229.9GB** 经 SHA 核对和完整解码验证 | | 精确恢复部分的校验和抽检 | 约 20 万个 4K 块，与 Btrfs CRC32C **全部一致** | | NoCOW 共享中快照前写入的数据 | 又找回约 **6,100 个文件 / 约 346GB**（另有约 3,800 个文件本地已有原件） | | 救不回的部分 | 1MiB 以下整文件加密的小文件、数据库文件、NoCOW 共享中快照后写入的文件 | ## 安装 使用 skills CLI： ```bash # 安装到当前项目 npx s

readme_excerpt: # sound 一个用于视频音效选材的 Claude Code Skill。从 Freesound 搜索和下载真实音效，结合下载量、评分人数、上传者描述、时长与许可证，帮助 Agent 为画面挑选合适的声音。 适用于转场、卡片入场、按钮点击、纸张滑动、碰撞等视频音效需求。Skill 的工作范围是音效搜索、筛选与下载；时长和能量分析可配合 FFmpeg 完成。 ## 安装 需要 Claude Code、Python 3，以及可访问 Freesound 的网络。搜索和下载脚本仅使用 Python 标准库，无需安装 Python 第三方依赖。 在项目根目录执行： ```bash git clone .claude/skills/sound ``` 核心文件： ```text .claude/skills/sound/ ├── SKILL.md # Agent 的技能入口与选材规则 ├── scripts/ │ ├── sfx.py # Freesound 搜索与下载 │ └── clash_freesound.py # 特定 ClashX Meta 环境的网络辅助脚本 └── references/ └── local-setup.md # 作者的本地网络配置参考 ``` ## 在 Claude Code 中使用 安装后，在视频项目中直接描述音效需求，例如： > 用 sound 帮我找一个卡片飞入时的短 whoosh，约 0.3 秒，适合轻快的产品演示，只选 CC0，下载到 sfx/。 > 给开关切换找一个柔和、不刺耳的点击音效。先给出候选、下载量、评分人数和试听链接。 Skill 引导 Agent： 1. 将画面动作转成英文关键词，在 Freesound 搜索候选。 2. 先判断声音来源、描述和时长是否符合画面，再参考下载量与评分人数，说明推荐依据。 3. 按使用需求筛选许可证；需要人工试听时提供预览链接。 4. 下载选中的音效，必要时用 FFmpeg 检查时长与能量分布，并保留所需署名信息。 下载量与评分只是选材线索，不代表声音一定适合当前画面；Agent 也不应把这些信号当作已经试听过的结论。 ## 直接运行脚本 脚本也可独立使用。以下命令均在项目根目录执行： ```bash S=.claude/skills/sound/scripts/sfx.py # 搜索 CC0 音效，并显示试听链接 python3 "$S" freesound "soft whoosh" --license cc0 --urls # 搜索纸张滑动，允许 CC0 和需要署名的 Attribution 音效 python3 "$S" freesound "paper slide" --license by -n 5 # 下载：把占位符替换为本次搜索返回的 fs:ID，可一次传入多个 python3 "$S" get sfx/ "fs: " "fs: " ``` 搜索结果会缓存在 `~/.cache/sfx-sources/index.json`。下载命令依赖这份缓存，因此需要先搜索，再使用结果中的 `fs:ID` 下载。当前下载的是 Freesound 的 MP3 预览文件，不是上传者的原始音频。 常用搜索参数： | 参数 | 作用 | | --- | --- | | `--license cc0` | 仅搜索 CC0 | | `--license by` | 搜索 CC0 和 Attribution | | `--license any` | 不过滤许可证，默认值 | | `--urls` | 显示试听链接 | | `-n 5` | 最多显示 5 条结果，默认 8 条 | | `--sort relevance` | 获取相关结果后按下载量重新排序，默认方式 | | `--sort downloads` / `rating` / `short` | 分别按下载量、评分或时长排序 | | `--pages 3` | 从起始页抓取的页数，默认 3 页 | | `-p 2` | 从第 2 页开始搜索，默认第 1 页 | ## 许可证与署名 每条音效的许可证可能不同。脚本支持按 CC0 或 Attribution 筛选；默认 `any` 也可能返回 BY-NC 等其他许

readme_excerpt: # neuron-lens What does each part of a large language model do? This project reads every MLP neuron and every attention head of two open models, Qwen3-8B (442,368 neurons, 1,152 heads) and Gemma 4 12B (737,280 neurons, 768 heads), three ways: from their weights alone, through two Jacobian lenses; from what they do on 15M tokens of real text; and from the exact tokens that drive them. Gemma 4 also takes images and sound, so its neurons are read through images and sound too. The result is a public catalog, the lenses that produced it, and measurements of where each way of reading works and where it fails. - **Lenses:** `stdlogits/rs-lenses`, the R-lens and S-lens for Qwen3-8B, and for Gemma 4 12B in text, images and sound. - **Catalog:** `stdlogits/neuron-lens`: every neuron's and head's reads, activation statistics, token drivers and legibility tests; labels in words; and for Gemma 4, what each neuron responds to in images and sound. - **Results:** docs/findings.md. **Methods:** docs/design.md. By @_a9lim and @treetowntree, with Claude. ## Background ### Neurons and heads A transformer keeps one vector per token, the *residual stream* (4,096 numbers in Qwen3-8B). Each of its 36 layers reads that stream and adds to it, in two steps: - **Attention heads move information between tokens.** At each position, a head looks back over the earlier tokens and copies something from them into the current one. Its *QK circuit* decides where it looks; its *OV circuit* decides what it copies. Qwen3-8B has 32 heads a layer. Head L20h17, for example, copies *she* forward and pushes against *he*. - **MLP neurons transform what is already there, one position at a time.** A neuron measures how strongly the stream points along a direction it reads (its *activation*), then adds a fixed vector

We call this **object-dependent concept brittleness** and show that it reflects systematic blind spots rather than sampling noise. Training a **sparse autoencoder (SAE) at every denoising step** makes abstract style and attribute concepts separable, so successful and failed generations can be compared, the missing, weakened or delayed concept dimensions located, and the failures **repaired at inference time** by nudging features toward a class-level concept prototype — no retraining. ## 🔍 Method - **Stage I — sparse prior construction in SAE space.** Classifier-free-guided step updates $\varepsilon_t$ are collected on training prompts, and one Top-$K$ SAE is trained per denoising step. readme_excerpt: # Clown Context Suite ComfyUI nodes for chaining MiniMax H3 clips without the quality slowly falling apart. ## Credits Clown Context Suite stands on the work of **seitanism** and **nikodemon**, who came before it. I'm just building off their work, so all credit to them for laying the groundwork. **Clowntext Hybrid Windows** is built on **kijai**'s MiniMax H3 context windows in ComfyUI and works the way **JalenBrunson**'s ComfyUI-HybridWindows does. All credit to them; I just added the keystone and capstone to it, to help everyone make longer videos without degradation. See Clowntext Hybrid Windows. **Clown Chain** is nikodemon's Chain node from ComfyUI-H3-Motion-Context, copied in and renamed (GPL-3.0, like this pack). See Clown Chain for why. ## The problem When you chain H3 clips, each new clip starts from the tail of the last one. You tell the model where to start, but never where to end. Detail is lost a little in every clip, and because each clip starts from the one before, the loss stacks up over the chain. ## The fix: Clown Keystone (recommended) Pull every shot back to clip 1. **Clown Context** pins the previous shot's tail to the front of each shot, so the motion carries over. **Clown Keystone** locks clip 1's first frame into the start of every shot and tacks clip 1's capstone onto the back, and **Clown Late Lock** brings the capstone in only for the last steps, so the shot picks its own pose first. Every shot is pulled back toward how clip 1 looked, so the loss can't stack up, and with Clown Context in front of Keystone the real frames are put back afterwards, so nothing from clip 1 ends up in the clips. readme_excerpt: # SameFace **ComfyUI nodes that measure where an image edit moved the parts of a face, and move them back.** Open weights, runs locally. **Can you spot the difference?** Lincoln's 1863 portrait and an edit that colourised and restored it, side by side at the same scale *Lincoln, 1863 (left), and an edit that colourised and restored it (right), lined up at the same scale. Hint: the head on the right is 3.7% wider for its height.* SameFace follows every point of a face from the original into the edit with optical flow (RAFT, inside a Grounded SAM 2 face mask), takes out the move, scale and turn of the whole face, and reports what is left - the drift - in % of face size, with plots of where it is. On the pair above it measured a drift of 0.83% of the head's size, and the 3.7% comes from the same measurement: to match the original, the edit's head had to be stretched 3.7% more in height than in width. **Ok, so what happened** Restore an old photo, colourise it, or ask an edit model for new hair or a new background, and the face often comes back slightly different: an eye a little higher, the jaw a little wider, the nose moved. You may sense that something changed, but not where or by how much - and because we recognise who a face belongs to so well, it still looks like the same person, so the change is easy to let pass. SameFace says where the face moved and how far, on one scale for every edit, and moves it back. It measures geometry - where the parts of the face went - not likeness. **Demo video** ## What it is for SameFace also moves the face back. readme_excerpt: # BlendGAN: Implicitly GAN Blending for Arbitrary Stylized Face Generation Official PyTorch implementation of the NeurIPS 2021 paper teaser Mingcong Liu, Qiang Li, Zekui Qin, Guoxin Zhang, Pengfei Wan, Wen Zheng Y-tech, Kuaishou Technology ### Project page | Paper Abstract: *Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have made a dramatic leap in high-fidelity image synthesis and stylized face generation. Recently, a layer-swapping mechanism has been developed to improve the stylization performance. However, this method is incapable of fitting arbitrary styles in a single model and requires hundreds of style-consistent training images for each style. To address the above issues, we propose BlendGAN for arbitrary stylized face generation by leveraging a flexible blending strategy and a generic artistic dataset. Specifically, we first train a self-supervised style encoder on the generic artistic dataset to extract the representations of arbitrary styles. In addition, a weighted blending module (WBM) is proposed to blend face and style representations implicitly and control the arbitrary stylization effect. By doing so, BlendGAN can gracefully fit arbitrary styles in a unified model while avoiding case-by-case preparation of style-consistent training images. To this end, we also present a novel large-scale artistic face dataset AAHQ. Extensive experiments demonstrate that BlendGAN outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of visual quality and style diversity for both latent-guided and reference-guided stylized face synthesis.* ### Updates :heavy_check_mark: (2021-12-03) The AAHQ dataset has been released! :heavy_check_mark: (2021-11-22) add an interactive demo based on Jupyter notebook :heavy_check_mark: (2021-11-19) a web demo is integrated to Huggingface Spaces with Grad

readme_excerpt: # SpEdE — Splat Edit Engine for ComfyUI Point at an object in a Gaussian-splat scene and ComfyUI takes it out: SAM 3.1 finds it in every capture camera, a visual hull collects its Gaussians and deletes them, Qwen-Image 2.1 paints the surface the object hid, MoGe-3 estimates the depth of that repaired view, and SpEdE aligns the depth to the scene and births new Gaussians only where the hole is. A further step makes the filled hole hold from every camera, not just the one you edited in. Or keep the object: **Extract** writes a clean object-only PLY. Or swap it: **Replace** has Qwen-Image 2.1 turbo draw a new object in its place, TripoSplat turn it into Gaussians and SpEdE stand it where the old one stood. Everything runs in your own ComfyUI on your own GPU. No cloud calls, no partner nodes, no bundled weights, no bundled scenes. Limits: SpEdE fills the support surface around the removed object (a tabletop, a floor, a wall, the things behind it that some camera saw). It is not general 3D inpainting and does not invent hidden objects. When the scene gives no trustworthy surface, the job fails closed instead of guessing. ## Why this is different - **The edit is in the scene, not on a picture.** Removal deletes the object's Gaussians; the fill births new Gaussians in the scene. They are anchored to MoGe-3 depth that is aligned to the scene's own rendered depth, so the result is a PLY you can walk around. - **Every step is judged by a gate.** G1 removal residual, G2 depth alignment (depth fill) or plane evidence (planar patch), G3 rendered patch against Qwen's edit, H1 other cameras unchanged outside the mask, K1 clean extraction. A failed gate stops the job and says why. - **The all-around fill makes the hole hold from every camera.** A repair that looks right in the hero cam

readme_excerpt: `oil-diff` 是一个 **Git 改动可视化汇报 Skill**。它把工作区修改、某次提交或分支之间的 Git Diff，按业务目的整理成 **3～7 件具体的事**，自动生成一份一屏看懂的 HTML 汇报页（`.oil-diff/index.html`）。 无论是向团队汇报一轮改动、合并代码前自己通览全局，还是想快速搞懂 AI 刚才改了什么，都不需要按字母顺序挨个翻几十个源码文件——打开网页，30 秒就能看清改了哪几块业务、为什么改、核心要看哪几个文件。 ## 核心功能 ### 1. 一屏 Bento 看板，按业务讲人话 不再按文件列表罗列改动，而是把整批修改归纳成几张清晰的业务卡片：顶部先给出一行模块导航，每张卡片用平实的话讲清「原来有什么痛点、现在怎么解决」，拒绝空洞的技术黑话。 ### 2. 配图是配图，文字是文字 每一章都配有直观的前后对比图，不用大段文字凑数： - **有界面改动时**：支持放入修改前后的真实运行截图，直接拖动滑杆对比或点击放大； - **纯逻辑或规则改动时**：自动生成路由分流图、控件前后对比、流程变化或字段增删表，一眼看懂机制变化。 ### 3. 按具体改动分类「🎯 核心必看」与「📎 外围同步」 一次改动涉及几十个文件时，自动帮你分好轻重缓急： - **🎯 核心必看**：直接归类挂在每章的 `1`、`2` 具体改动点下方，标明增删行数，告诉你 Review 时最该看哪几个文件； - **📎 外围同步**：顺手同步修改的引用、配置或文档自动折叠收在卡片底部，不抢视线、也不漏文件。 ### 4. 可收起文件树 + 右侧滑出代码抽屉 右侧配有紧凑的改动文件树（支持一键收起释放全宽画布）。想看某处具体改了哪几行代码时，点一下「核心必看」文件胶囊或右侧文件树，右侧立即滑出修改前后代码对照抽屉，主页面原地不动、不乱滚。 ## 安装与使用 ### 安装 **方式一 · 命令行安装** ```bash npx skills add oil-oil/oil-diff ``` **方式二 · 直接发给 Agent 安装** ```text 请帮我安装这个 Skill： ``` ### 日常使用 安装后，直接在对话里告诉 Agent 你想看哪部分改动即可： ```text 用 oil-diff 把当前分支最近的改动做成汇报页。 ``` ```text 用 oil-diff 整理目前还没提交的修改，生成一份 HTML 改动汇报。 ``` ```text 用 oil-diff 对比 main..HEAD 的改动，看看这轮到底改了哪几件事。 ``` ## 适用边界、数据与运行环境 - **零污染仓库状态**：生成的网页与数据全部放在 ` /.oil-diff/` 目录下，并自动对 Git 隐形，不修改项目原本的任何文件，也不影响 `git status`。 - **单文件离线可用**：最终生成的 `.oil-diff/index.html` 是零外部依赖的单文件网页，双击就能在浏览器打开，也可以直接发给同事查看。 - **配置与兼容性**：无需额外配置 API Key 或环境变量；仅依赖系统 `git` 与 Python 3.10+ 标准库，支持 macOS、Windows 与 Linux。 ## 许可证 MIT License

Same prompt and seed. A de-roped Pika clip takes about as long as one 25-step base render (about 6 min at 1280x704 on one RTX PRO 6000 Max-Q) and comes out with more motion and crisper frames. ▶ Full video with timings, motion and sharpness · workflows - **No training, no reference images, no rendering** needed to make a dial. readme_excerpt: # mv-director · 让 AI 读懂歌词、卡准节拍，用代码做音乐 MV 给 Codex、Claude Code 这类 AI 编程助手用的 skill。你给它一首歌和歌词，它会： 1. **听懂音乐**：把歌分成鼓、人声等几条音轨，找出每一拍、每个小节、副歌和抽鼓；用对齐模型把每个字的开唱时间对到大约 0.1 秒。 2. **读懂歌词**：先写清楚这首歌在讲什么、主角是谁、情绪怎么走，再逐句写分镜，每句画面演出这句在说什么。 3. **用你选的画风来画**：可以借 lemo-opuscar、花叔 huashu-art-motion 这些风格库里的画风（换别的风格库也行）。它会先翻一遍有哪些画风，推荐几个最配这首歌的，问你要哪个。 4. **卡点、渲染、审片**：镜头切在小节头上，进副歌那一拍画面炸开，字在唱出来那一刻出现；渲出 1080p 60 帧，再从成片画面里量一遍字对不对得上、画面跟没跟拍，不合格自己改。 画面全部用代码画（HTML Canvas 逐帧渲染），不用生图。 ## 安装 ### 1. 装环境 需要 Python 3.9+ 和 ffmpeg，然后： ```bash python -m pip install numpy scipy matplotlib pillow playwright demucs torch transformers python -m playwright install chromium ``` - `demucs`：分轨，推荐装。 - `torch` + `transformers`：逐字对齐，强烈推荐装。有 NVIDIA 显卡就装 CUDA 版 torch，没有也能用 CPU。 - 对齐模型第一次用时会自动下载约 1.8 GB；国内先设 `HF_ENDPOINT= 装完在 skill 文件夹里跑一次 `python -I scripts/doctor.py`，它会告诉你还缺什么。详细说明见 references/安装.md。 ### 2. 装 skill 在 Codex 里发： ``` $skill-installer 安装 在仓库根目录，安装时用 --path . --name mv-director） ``` 也可以自己克隆： ```bash git clone ~/.agents/skills/mv-director # Codex git clone ~/.claude/skills/mv-director # Claude Code ``` 装好后**新开一个对话**。 ### 3. 准备一个风格库（可选） 想借画风，就把风格库下到你的工作文件夹，比如： ```bash git clone ``` 花叔的 huashu-art-motion 可以按它的说明装成 skill，也可以 clone 下来。别的风格库也行，只要里面有画风说明。 ## 用法：提示词模板 工作文件夹里放好歌（mp3 / wav）和歌词（带时间的 `.lrc` 最好；一行一句的纯文本 `.txt` 也行），然后对 AI 说： **让它翻风格库、推荐几个给你选** ``` 用 mv-director 给 song.mp3 做一支 MV，做 30 秒左右，你挑最有戏的一段。 歌是 的《 》，歌词在 lyrics.lrc。 画风从 lemo-opuscar 里挑：先翻一遍它有哪些画风，按这首歌推荐几个给我选，我选好你再做。 ``` 它会列出推荐和全部画风，然后问你。你回一句就行： ``` 就用 。 ``` **换成花叔的画风库** ``` ……画风从花叔的 huashu-art-motion 里挑：先翻一遍有哪些画风，推荐几个给我选。 ``` **换成别的风格库** ``` ……画风参考 ：先看懂它的画风是怎么组织的，推荐几个给我选。 ``` **直接指定画风，不用问** ``` ……画风用 lemo-opuscar 的 ink-wash（中国水墨）。 ``` **指定段落** ``` ……只做 0:45 到 1:20 这一段。 ``` 成片在项目文件夹的 `out/mv.mp4`，制作记录在 `NOTES.md`。 ## 它和别的 MV skill 有什么不一样 我们读过、跑过十来个开源的 MV / 画风

readme_excerpt: # ComfyUI-Open-H3-Regenerate ComfyUI nodes and workflows for NVIDIA's **Open-H3-Regenerate-2K**, the open replacement for the closed MiniMax H3-Regenerate-2K API. It takes a low-resolution draft (an H3 768P render, or a 384P–576P clip from LTX, Wan, SANA-Video…) and regenerates it **natively at 768P, 1080P, 2K or 4K in three diffusion steps**, on ComfyUI's native MiniMax H3 model. ``` draft ─► H3 VAE encode ─► H3-Latent-Upscaler (LBH 3D) onto the target grid ─► re-noise to σ 0.909375 ─► 3 Euler steps (0.909375 → 0.857 → 0.667 → 0), CFG 1 FL2VA + merged LoRA (refiner + LightX2V FL2VA Turbo + LMS Sharp) + 50 Sharp curve branches, audio held as encoded silence ─► fast H3 VAE decoder (StreamRender-H3) ``` The pipeline follows NVIDIA's reference code (NVlabs/Sana, `models/Open-H3-Regenerate-2K`). It also adds **Video to H3 Prompt**, which writes an H3 prompt for any clip with a vision model on your own OpenAI-compatible server. ## Install ```bash cd ComfyUI/custom_nodes git clone ``` Also install Comfyui_Minimax_h3_latent_Upscaler (the latent upscaler node). Restart ComfyUI. Needs ComfyUI with native MiniMax H3 support (tested on 0.42.0). ### Models | File | Put it in | Download | |---|---|---| | `open_h3_regenerate_2k_lora.safetensors` (12.4 GB) | `models/loras/` | Efficient-Large-Model/Open-H3-Regenerate-2K `lora/` | | `sharp_curve_branches.safetensors` (1.2 GB) | `models/loras/` | same, `lora/` | | `fast_h3_vae_noncausal_24l.safetensors` (6.5 GB) | `models/vae/` | same, `vae_fast/` | | `minimax_h3_latent_upscaler_3d_conv_v1_*` | `models/latent_upscale_models/` | same, `latent_upsampler/` (or LBH-123-AI's release) | | MiniMax H3 **FL2VA** model (any variant; the reference base is FL2VA) | `models/diffusion_models/` | Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3 | | a **pruned ref2va** checkpoint

readme_excerpt: # ComfyUI Open-H3 Face Region Keep the face when you regenerate MiniMax H3 videos to 2K. NVIDIA's Open-H3-Regenerate-2K upscales a 768p H3 clip and re-draws it at 2560x1440 from a start noise of 0.909. That adds a lot of detail, but it also re-draws the people: in my tests the face in the 2K clip matched the draft at only 0.52 (ArcFace cosine). These nodes add an automatic face mask so faces start the 2K pass from lower noise (0.50) while the rest of the frame still gets the full regenerate. Same clip, same seed: face match 0.91, lip sync kept, 10.8x the detail of a plain upscale. Workflows and the full write-up: BennyDaBall/MiniMax-H3-Workflows. ## Nodes | Node | What it does | |---|---| | **Open-H3 Face Region Map** | Finds faces in every draft frame (OpenCV YuNet, CPU, a few seconds per clip), adds any manual boxes (pets, props), maps them onto the 2K latent grid with H3's frame grouping, pads and feathers them, and saves a strength map (.npy in `output/open_h3_masks`). `face_strength` 0.55 with NVIDIA's 0.909 start = faces start at 0.50. | | **Open-H3 Region Noise** | Noise source for SamplerCustomAdvanced: each token starts at `(1 - m*s)*draft + m*s*noise`, where m is the map. | | **Open-H3 Region Strength** | Model patch: passes the map to H3 as its per-token video denoise mask, so each region follows its own schedule `m * sigma` at every step. | Use **Region Noise** and **Region Strength** together with the same map. readme_excerpt: # FastDialogueSidon ![Model]( Backends GPU ![DialogueSidon]( License ## Introduction **FastDialogueSidon** is a fast one-step model for full-duplex two-speaker dialogue separation and joint restoration: a raw 16 kHz mono mixture (telephone / conversational audio, up to 120 s per window) goes in, two separated 24 kHz speaker tracks come out. Every module — encoder, DiT head and decoder — is trained for FastDialogueSidon. A single DiT step per window replaces the 30 diffusion steps of DialogueSidon, and a **lightweight decoder** (a frame-rate SAN-WaveNeXt2 (WaveFitNeXt) latent decoder, 30 M parameters) replaces its DAC decoder. Running on fused GPU kernels, it is **~100x faster** than the official DialogueSidon release run as-is, at matching intelligibility. FastDialogueSidon architecture Two interchangeable backends share the same weights and the same Python interface (`separate`, `separate_batch`, `stream_files`): - **`triton/`** — Triton kernels around cuBLAS, no engine build, fp16 by default. readme_excerpt: # ComfyUI-MOSS-QwenVL-Layout A ComfyUI node that turns a reference image into a **MOSS-Image layout prompt**. Qwen3-VL / Qwen3.5-VL looks at your image, finds the things you ask for (including text, if you ask), and the node writes the layout JSON that MOSS-Image expects: captions, text content and bounding boxes converted to MOSS's `abs_centralized` / `yxyx` coordinate format. There are two modes. **From image** (default) detects and captions a reference image. **From prompt (experimental)** needs no image: you write a prompt and Qwen designs the whole box layout for it. You can also add **change requests** ("make the dress red", "replace the man with an elderly woman in a grey coat", "add a dog on the left"). The captions are then written to describe the *edited* result, so MOSS generates the changed version while keeping the original composition. > Unofficial community node. readme_excerpt: # `okf` In 2026 Google published the Open Knowledge Format (OKF), an open way to write knowledge down so that people and AI models read the same files. This project is research into an implementation of OKF that works in real life, and above all inside a company, where the material is messy, the readers are many, the rules change each year, and a wrong answer has a cost. It tries to answer the questions an organization asks before it lets an AI model answer for it: - Which knowledge, and for whom? - Where does each answer come from, and can a person check it? - Who confirmed it, and is it still true? - What happens when two documents disagree? - How does a correction found by a user reach the knowledge? - Who may see what? People want to ask a question in plain words and get an answer they can act on. Language models answer fluently. They also **invent facts**, cannot say where an answer comes from, and cannot tell a current rule from one that was replaced years ago. Method Reference · Examples OpenPPI is a Python library for prediction-powered inference: valid confidence intervals that combine a small labeled sample with predictions from a fixed machine-learning model. It implements representative methods for passive PPI (labeled and unlabeled samples given) and for active inference (the method chooses which units to label under a budget), validated against published formulas and, where available, official code. The `LabelShift` extension additionally supports different source and target label distributions under an invariant `X|Y` model. Each method is a **sampling component** (which rows to label) combined with an **inference component** (estimate and interval); `openppi.methods` records the published combinations, so `get_method('ASI')` returns its parts. Every inference component inherits from `InferenceMethod`, takes a validated data snapshot and returns an `InferenceResult` with the estimate, standard error, confidence interval and diagnostics. The core depends only on NumPy and SciPy. Unsloth's UD-Q4_K_XL in prod; Q8_0 runs too with part of its experts in RAM. **Every layer is split across all three cards**, so one request reads weights from all three cards' memory at the same time. Splitting by layers — llama.cpp's default — passes one small activation per card boundary and works over any link, but for one request the cards take turns: two of three idle. readme_excerpt: # academic-revision-checklist 给英文学术写作用的修改清单：66 条规则，16 条快速清单，一套「一个案例，一条规则，查全文」的做法，和一个列候选的脚本。 这些规则来自我的英文博士论文（人机交互方向，2026 年 10 月通过答辩）五周、60 多轮的修改记录。每一条都是先在一个具体的句子上卡住，修好，再抽象成一条能拿去检查的规则，然后带着它把全文查一遍。 可以直接当清单读，也可以装成 Claude 的 skill，让 Claude 按这套做法逐句帮你查。 English summary ## 「AI 痕迹」指什么 这里说的「AI 痕迹」，跟检测器查不查得出来没多大关系。它指的是读者第一次读就卡住、要回头再读一遍的地方。导师、委员会、审稿人读到这种地方，就会觉得是机器写的。 学校或期刊要求说明 AI 用在了哪里，就照规定写清楚。 ## 十六条快速清单 改完一段，逐条问一遍。 1. 第一次读的人会在这一句停下吗？要读两遍的，写下原因。 2. 一句话只报一个结果。 3. 写了 more、higher，就写出和谁比。 4. significant 只用在差异、关联或检验上，不用在比例或平均数上。 5. this、these、the former、the name 这类词，指的东西在前一句之内吗？ 6. 一个名字只指一样东西，普通词别撞上自己定义的术语。 7. 冒号只用来引出列表、引文、问题或定义。 8. 少用先否定再肯定的铺垫，带内容的否定留下。 9. 正文不用破折号连接分句。 10. 连着几句长度差不多、开头一样的，改掉一处。 11. 空的过渡词和段尾总结，能删就删，删不掉就换成具体内容。 12. 用自己和这个领域会用的词，能用常用词就不用生僻词。 13. 论文只写研究本身，不写论文是怎么改出来的。 14. 研究问题、引文、数字、自己的反思，不交给 AI 改。 15. 改完重读这一段和前一段，字数上限、段落长度这些硬指标再跑一遍。 16. 别人和 AI 的意见，先拿原文和数据对过，成立的才改。 66 条的完整版在 `references/checklist.md`，每条一句话；规则、改前改后的原句和查法在 `references/patterns.md`，编号一致。 ## 文件 ```text academic-revision-checklist/ ├── README.md 就是这个文件 ├── SKILL.md 给 Claude 的说明（英文） ├── LICENSE ├── references/ │ ├── checklist.md 16 条快速清单和 66 条一句话规则，从这里开始 │ ├── patterns.md 66 条的完整版：规则、论文里真改过的句子、怎么查 │ ├── workflow.md 一轮修改怎么走，外部意见怎么核对，给其他模型的提示词 │ ├── reading-protocols.md 像第一次读的人那样读，标题怎么读，出声读 │ └── lessons.md 九条原则和八条教训 └── scripts/ └── flag_candidates.py 列出脚本找得到的候选：破折号、冒号、对比句式等 ``` 规则和说明是中文写的，例子都是英文原句。 ## 怎么用 ### 1. 当清单读 从 `references/checklist.md` 开始。想知道某一条为什么要改、怎么改，就看 `patterns.md` 里同一个编号。 ### 2. 装成 Claude Code 的 skill ```bash git clone ~/.claude/skills/academic-revision-checklist ``` 然后在 Claude Code 里说「用 academic-revision-checklist 检查 chapter3.tex」，或者输入 `/academic-revision-checklist`。只想在一个项目里用，就放到那个项目的 `.claude/skills/` 下面。 ### 3. 在 Claude 网页版或桌面版里用 把整个文件夹打包成 zip，作为自定义 skill 上传，步骤见 Claude 帮助中心的 Use skills in Claude

For inference: - parameter estimation using least squares estimation, maximum likelihood estimation (MLE), and maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation; - physically-constrained deep learning using differentiable simulation, with neural networks embedded inside the physical model. readme_excerpt: AREALS Learn surface geometry. Transfer the representation to pressure prediction. Demo · Models · Pretraining · WindsorML · Citation AREALS learns from geometry alone. Pretraining encodes complete surfaces and predicts the unsigned distance and the unoriented normal at arbitrary query points; fine-tuning on WindsorML reuses the encoder and the query decoder to predict surface pressure. **74.5% fewer simulations.** Fine-tuned AREALS matches the accuracy of the same architecture trained from scratch with 74.5% fewer simulations on WindsorML and 50% fewer on DrivAerML and DrivAerNet++ (paper). The 6.4M checkpoint `areals-6.4m` reaches the WindsorML target with **86.9% fewer**. - **Spatial tokens.** Each of 256 tokens sits at an anchor (a farthest-point sample of the surface) and attends to the surface samples with weights proportional to their area. - **Spatial queries.** A query at any world position reads the tokens through area-weighted cross-attention with 3D rotary positions. Queries never attend to each other. - **Unoriented normals.** The decoder predicts the projector *nnᵀ*, which does not change when *n* flips sign. - **Analytic candidates.** Per query, the geometry decoder blends learned distance and normal heads with an analytic *surfel readout*: the distance to the nearest of 2,048 small disks through surface samples. It also blends the same readout taken through up to 16 rigid symmetry maps of the input. The readout has no learned weights and is close to exact on densely sampled surfaces; learned gates set each candidate's weight (`model.py`). - **Transfer.** The pressure model fine-tunes the encoder and the query decoder and reads the decoder's query features with a new linear head; it does not use the readout or the geometry heads. ## Install Python 3.10–3.

A CLI that finds early-stage startups, reads their website with an LLM, finds a founder's email, and saves a personalized plain-text cold email to your **Gmail Drafts** for you to review and send yourself. readme_excerpt: # neuron-lens What does each part of a large language model do? This project reads every MLP neuron and every attention head of two open models, Qwen3-8B (442,368 neurons, 1,152 heads) and Gemma 4 12B (737,280 neurons, 768 heads), three ways: from their weights alone, through two Jacobian lenses; from what they do on 15M tokens of real text; and from the exact tokens that drive them. Gemma 4 also takes images and sound, so its neurons are read through images and sound too. The result is a public catalog, the lenses that produced it, and measurements of where each way of reading works and where it fails. - **Lenses:** `stdlogits/rs-lenses`, the R-lens and S-lens for Qwen3-8B, and for Gemma 4 12B in text, images and sound. - **Catalog:** `stdlogits/neuron-lens`: every neuron's and head's reads, activation statistics, token drivers and legibility tests; labels in words; and for Gemma 4, what each neuron responds to in images and sound. - **Results:** docs/findings.md. **Methods:** docs/design.md. Novel view synthesis and 3D reconstruction have advanced rapidly with radiance fields and splatting, yet their memory and computational demands limit their use in resource-constrained settings. We introduce Hexels: novel planar hexagonal surface elements with a first-order spatial color field for efficient 3D scene and 2D image representation. Hexels exploit locally planar regions with smoothly varying appearance using fewer, larger primitives. readme_excerpt: # netprobe — CVE-2026-98432 Hello. CVE-2026-98432 is remotely exploitable Use-After-Free in the Linux Kernel. Some reporting states that AI labs exploited it after ~45min via Multi-Path TCP (MPTCP). The vulnerability is actually in the IPv4 TCP stack itself, it's just that MPTCP is the only even remotely practical way to reach the vulnerable code path. Even then, ~45min should receive a very deep squint of scrutiny. * The vulnerable interval is fixed by the code at roughly the distance between the `ireq_opt` load and the first dereference. * The free is 100 µs to milliseconds later (accept + close). * It is not enough for an interrupt to land in the window; the CPU must **stay away from the reader for longer than the free latency**. * On a normal (!PREEMPT_RT) kernel, softirqs are not scheduled at all and even a flood of hard IRQs would still finish in about 10ns, long before the free needed to hit a use-after-free. * The duplicate SYN and the ACK carry the same 4-tuple, so RSS/RPS/sk_incoming_cpu place them in the same receive queue and process them on the same CPU. Said another way: Softirqs on a CPU are serialized and due to flow affinity, there is not reader left to race for the UAF. There are surely custom linux kernels which use MPTCP with per-packet steering options which likely make this vulnerability "reachable" in the purest sense. Practically speaking, you are almost certainly not running such a kernel configuration, and also aren't that unllucky for someone to be latency-close-enough and persistent enough to shoot that gap. readme_excerpt: 人类梗知识库 · Human Meme KB 哈基米在 B 站评论区秒接梗，靠的是这本书。 一只猫读不完人类的梗——那就全人类一起写。 用你的 AI 读它 · 投喂一个梗 · 里面有什么 · 给 AI agent 用 · 投喂名单 --- ## 用你的 AI 读它 把仓库下载到电脑上，在这个文件夹里打开你的 AI 编程助手（Claude Code、Codex、Cursor、Gemini CLI 都行），它会自己读仓库里的说明： ```sh git clone cd human-meme-kb ``` 没装 git 的话，点页面上方绿色的 **Code → Download ZIP**，解压后打开那个文件夹也一样。 然后直接跟它说，比如： > 这是啥？我能拿它做什么？ > > "断不了情根"是什么梗？哈基米会怎么接？ > > 评论区有人回我"这里不送猫娘"，这是什么意思？ 这里只有文字，没有要运行的程序。问梗、查出处，你的 AI 只需要读文件；只有你让它投喂时，它才会上网查证、写文件、在 GitHub 上帮你提交。 ## 投喂一个梗 格式很简单，三样东西： ```text 梗：断不了情根 出处：抖音 AI 视频模板 怎么接：先看清照片里是谁 ``` 收录后会署上你的昵称。三种投喂方式，挑一个顺手的： ### 1. 让你的 AI 帮你提交（一句话） 在 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor 这类能用终端的 AI agent 里说： > 帮我把"梗名"这个梗投喂到 Hajimi0721owo/human-meme-kb，出处是……，一般这样接：……，署名写"你的昵称"。 它会读仓库里的 AGENTS.md，自己上网核实出处、查重、按格式写好、做安全自查、跑检查、提 PR，最后把链接给你。你说得不全也没关系，它会去查。电脑上装了 GitHub CLI 并登录过（`gh auth login`）最顺；没有的话，它会给你一个填好的投喂表链接，点一下提交就行。 ### 2. 填表 点这里打开投喂表，填梗、出处、怎么接，提交就好。维护者会帮你整理进库。 ### 3. 自己提 PR 复制 `memes/_TEMPLATE.md` 成 `memes/梗名.md`，填好（记得在"来源"里放链接）后跑一下检查再提交： ```sh python3 tools/check_meme.py memes/梗名.md ``` 范例：`memes/断不了情根.md`。 > 评论区直接留言也算投喂，会尽量收录。 ## 里面有什么 | 位置 | 内容 | | --- | --- | | `memes/` | **社区投喂的梗**，一梗一文件：是什么、怎么接、例句 | | `meme-lab/` | 四卷梗考据：DeepSeek 社区名场面、技术梗、大厂互动梗、全网经典梗 | ## 给 AI agent 用 加载知识库、帮用户一句话投喂（上网核实 → 写条目 → 安全自查 → 格式检查 → 提 PR）的完整说明都在 AGENTS.md。 ## 收录规则 - 一个梗一个文件，写短写准，附上来源链接；查不到的写"待核实"，不编。 - 条目会被 AI 当资料读，所以只写对梗的描述：不写给 AI 的指令、不藏文字、不放要人运行的命令。每个 PR 都会自动检查。 - 不收任何人的真实姓名、联系方式等个人信息；只收文字，不收图片。 - 已经收录过的梗，请补充原条目，不要重复新建。 ## 致谢与许可 - AI 娘角色原案来自 B 站画师 @ZipZipPipe，角色与设定归原作者所有。 - 每一位投喂者都记在 CONTRIBUTORS.md。 - 本仓库的文字内容以 CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 共享：转载请署名、非商业、相同方式共享。第三方作品与商标说明见 THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md。

readme_excerpt: **中文** | English | 日本語 | 한국어 # oracle-snatch 一个小的 Python 循环脚本：不停用甲骨文云的官方接口申请免费 ARM 实例（VM.Standard.A1.Flex），直到哪次赶上放货、接口点头为止。 ## 为什么写这个 Always Free 的 A1.Flex 免费额度（总共 4 核 / 24 GB）是目前最划算的免费服务器，没有之一。问题是热门区域在控制台里基本永远显示「Out of host capacity」（没货）。这个货不是永久没了，而是会不定期放出来一小波，没人通知。对着控制台刷一周刷新纯属浪费生命，不如让脚本替你去问。 2026 年 10 月我用一个粗糙版本在东京区域跑了好几天。日志翻来覆去就是「没货」，中间还因为我把间隔设得太密、吃过几次 429 限流。最后抢到了那台 4 核 24 GB 的机器，我现在自托管的大部分服务都跑在它上面，到今天账单还是 0。这个仓库就是那个循环的整理版，配置都抽了出来。 ## 它做什么 - 只用甲骨文官方 API（Python 的 `oci` SDK），不搞控制台自动化、不模拟浏览器。 - 轮询你所在区域的每一个可用域（AD），每轮每个 AD 尝试一次。东京只有一个 AD，多 AD 的区域中签率会好一些。 - 「没货」就当「还没到时候」：歇一会儿，下一个 AD，下一轮。 - 遇到 429 限流就长退避（默认 300 秒）。硬顶着 429 往前冲，只会让限流赖着不走。 - 遇到配额错误（LimitExceeded）直接停，并把原因写清楚：这说明你的免费额度已经用完了，再重试一万次也没用。 - 抢到后等实例变成 RUNNING，拿到公网 IP，写进 `snatched.json`，可选发一条 Telegram 通知，然后退出。 - `--dry-run` 只验证配置：列出可用域、确认会用哪个镜像，不真开机器。第一次先跑这个。 它不做的事：不帮你注册账号、不建 VCN、不生成 API 密钥，更变不出不存在的货。它只是替你不知疲倦地问。 ## 安装与使用 需要一个甲骨文云账号，以及 OCI 的配置文件（`~/.oci/config`，里面配好 API 密钥）。用过 OCI CLI 或 SDK 的人都有这个文件。 还需要一个子网 OCID：控制台里 Networking -> Virtual Cloud Networks -> 你的 VCN -> Subnets。想要公网 IP 就选公有子网（你肯定想要）。 ```bash git clone cd oracle-snatch pip install -r requirements.txt cp config.example.env config.env # 改 config.env：必填的只有 SUBNET_ID 和 SSH_PUBLIC_KEY_FILE python3 snatch.py --dry-run python3 snatch.py ``` ## 长期挂着跑 这东西就是设计成无人值守跑好几天的，所以挂在任何一台你已有的常开机器上就行（别处的免费小鸡、家里的服务器、树莓派都可以）。仓库里附了一个 systemd 服务示例： ```bash sudo cp oracle-snatch.service /etc/systemd/system/ sudo systemctl enable --now oracle-snatch tail -f snatch.log ``` ## 踩过的坑 - 免费 A1 额度是总量，不是每台一份：一共 4 核 + 24 GB。可以开一台 4/24，也可以拆成两台 2/12。超了就是 LimitExceeded，脚本会主动停，别怪它。 - 账号升级成 PAYG（按量付费）不会吃掉免费额度，额度内的 A1 用量照样不收钱，体感上货还稍微多一点。我的账号就是 PAYG，账单至今 0 元，另外设了个预算警报兜底。 - 启动盘也算在 200 GB 免费块存储总量里。50 GB 对小服务器足够了，别因为「反正免费」默认拉满 200，剩下的额度留给第二台更划算。 - 放货时间没规律，经常在半夜。循环的意义就在这：凌晨 4 点它醒着，你不用。 - 别把重试间隔改成几秒。你不会

Аналог ESP32 с ESPHome: колонка используется только как железо (микрофоны, динамик и слово активации «Алиса» работают прямо на ней), а вся обработка речи и ответы идут у вас дома. Облако Яндекса не нужно. - **Голос:** «Алиса, …» → Vosk → встроенный Assist HA → TTS. Без LLM. Для озвучки рекомендуем Silero: он звучит заметно живее Piper, который работает по умолчанию. - **Информер:** `tts.speak` на `media_player.alisa`. - **Плеер:** файлы и TTS из HA, интернет-радио через прокси моста, громкость, пауза. - **Управление мостом:** датчики «Мост» и «Колонка на связи», кнопка «Перезапустить мост», выбор движков речи (TTS и STT) прямо в HA. - **Приватность:** интернет колонке закрыт, облако Яндекса заменено мостом в вашем контейнере. > **Отказ от ответственности.** Неофициальный проект, не связан с Яндексом. Он даёт root-доступ к вашей колонке и отключает обновления. Всё на ваш риск: колонку можно «окирпичить», гарантия теряется. Делайте только со своим устройством. ## Как это работает ``` Станция Мини (root, /etc/hosts → мост) │ uniproxy (protobuf по WSS :443), HTTP quasar/* :80/:443 ▼ Мост alice-ha = quasard + патчи (LXC на Proxmox) │ REST: /api/stt/stt.vosk → /api/conversation/process → /api/tts_get_url (tts.piper) ▼ Home Assistant └─ интеграция noema_alice → media_player.alisa → мост /_play /_cmd → glagol колонки :1961 ``` Колонка сама распознаёт слово «Алиса» и шлёт звук на мост по протоколу Яндекса. Мост переводит его в запросы к REST API HA и возвращает ответ. В обратную сторону HA управляет колонкой через мост и её локальный API glagol. Подробности: docs/architecture.md. ## Что понадобится Колонку не нужно разбирать.

readme_excerpt: # SpEdE — Splat Edit Engine for ComfyUI Point at an object in a Gaussian-splat scene and ComfyUI takes it out: SAM 3.1 finds it in every capture camera, a visual hull collects its Gaussians and deletes them, Qwen-Image 2.1 paints the surface the object hid, MoGe-3 estimates the depth of that repaired view, and SpEdE aligns the depth to the scene and births new Gaussians only where the hole is. A further step makes the filled hole hold from every camera, not just the one you edited in. Or keep the object: **Extract** writes a clean object-only PLY. Or swap it: **Replace** has Qwen-Image 2.1 turbo draw a new object in its place, TripoSplat turn it into Gaussians and SpEdE stand it where the old one stood. Everything runs in your own ComfyUI on your own GPU. No cloud calls, no partner nodes, no bundled weights, no bundled scenes. Limits: SpEdE fills the support surface around the removed object (a tabletop, a floor, a wall, the things behind it that some camera saw). It is not general 3D inpainting and does not invent hidden objects. When the scene gives no trustworthy surface, the job fails closed instead of guessing. ## Why this is different - **The edit is in the scene, not on a picture.** Removal deletes the object's Gaussians; the fill births new Gaussians in the scene. They are anchored to MoGe-3 depth that is aligned to the scene's own rendered depth, so the result is a PLY you can walk around. - **Every step is judged by a gate.** G1 removal residual, G2 depth alignment (depth fill) or plane evidence (planar patch), G3 rendered patch against Qwen's edit, H1 other cameras unchanged outside the mask, K1 clean extraction. NVIDIA's Open-H3-Regenerate-2K upscales a 768p H3 clip and re-draws it at 2560x1440 from a start noise of 0.909. readme_excerpt: # OpenBonsai **Research preview.** The method was measured end to end on Qwen3.5-9B, first with the research scripts and then with the package's own `openbonsai run`, and on Qwen3-8B through the generic dense adapter. The results are early and the evaluation is small. The current model is on Hugging Face: webbrain-one/openbonsai-qwen-3.5-9b. It was calibrated on Qwen3.5-9B's own math and code answers, with extra code, and is still below the official Ternary Bonsai: with thinking off, 65/100 on GSM8K and 34/50 on HumanEval, against 77/100 and 45/50; with thinking on, the chat template's default, 32/50 and 14/25, against 46/50 and 24/25 (see Results). The HumanEval score is probably optimistic: the setting was picked from four runs scored on the same 50 problems, and its training prompts restate at least 6 of them in other words (More code in the data). It replaced the first release on 29 October 2026; the first release, with less code in its data, stays there at revision `40964de`, tag `reasoning-mix-v1`. Independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Prism ML. Bonsai is Prism ML's product. OpenBonsai is an open (Apache-2.0) framework that compresses a dense language model to ternary weights in the format of Prism ML's Ternary Bonsai models: Prism's PTQ1_0 GGUF, which runs in Prism's llama.cpp fork. For Qwen3.5-9B the output is a file of about 2 GB, with the same tensor layout as Ternary-Bonsai-2-9B. **Why.** Prism publishes finished Bonsai weights for the base models it chooses, and an inference runtime. The view moves at once over a panorama of everything the camera can see, and the camera follows. When it gets there, the live picture lands exactly where the view is. It's self-contained. You need the camera's ONVIF login, nothing else: no Frigate, no other camera integration. > Status: early proof of concept. Tested with one camera (a Dahua SD49225DB-HNY). ## What it does - **Camera entity.** A camera entity streams the camera's RTSP feed, so Home Assistant's built-in WebRTC (go2rtc) plays it. - **One calibration pass** (a few minutes; the camera moves around and comes back): 1. Measures how far a frame spans at a few zooms. 2. Fits the camera's geometry: degrees per pan / tilt unit, the focal length at each zoom, and the lens's distortion. 3. Sweeps the whole range at the widest zoom and stitches it into one panorama. - **The `ptz-360-card` card:** draws the panorama and the live picture through the camera's lens model (WebGL). It finds every frame of a move in the one before (normalised correlation, in a Web Worker), checks it against the panorama, and finds frames again after the video stalls (it does). The panorama is repainted from what the camera has seen where it stopped, kept in your browser. ## Install 1. Enter the camera's address, ONVIF port and login. 3. Add the card to a dashboard: ```yaml type: custom:ptz-360-card entity: camera.your_camera ``` 4. The card offers to **Calibrate** (admins only). readme_excerpt: `oil-diff` 是一个 **Git 改动可视化汇报 Skill**。它把工作区修改、某次提交或分支之间的 Git Diff，按业务目的整理成 **3～7 件具体的事**，自动生成一份一屏看懂的 HTML 汇报页（`.oil-diff/index.html`）。 无论是向团队汇报一轮改动、合并代码前自己通览全局，还是想快速搞懂 AI 刚才改了什么，都不需要按字母顺序挨个翻几十个源码文件——打开网页，30 秒就能看清改了哪几块业务、为什么改、核心要看哪几个文件。 ## 核心功能 ### 1. 一屏 Bento 看板，按业务讲人话 不再按文件列表罗列改动，而是把整批修改归纳成几张清晰的业务卡片：顶部先给出一行模块导航，每张卡片用平实的话讲清「原来有什么痛点、现在怎么解决」，拒绝空洞的技术黑话。 ### 2. 配图是配图，文字是文字 每一章都配有直观的前后对比图，不用大段文字凑数： - **有界面改动时**：支持放入修改前后的真实运行截图，直接拖动滑杆对比或点击放大； - **纯逻辑或规则改动时**：自动生成路由分流图、控件前后对比、流程变化或字段增删表，一眼看懂机制变化。 ### 3. 按具体改动分类「🎯 核心必看」与「📎 外围同步」 一次改动涉及几十个文件时，自动帮你分好轻重缓急： - **🎯 核心必看**：直接归类挂在每章的 `1`、`2` 具体改动点下方，标明增删行数，告诉你 Review 时最该看哪几个文件； - **📎 外围同步**：顺手同步修改的引用、配置或文档自动折叠收在卡片底部，不抢视线、也不漏文件。 ### 4. 可收起文件树 + 右侧滑出代码抽屉 右侧配有紧凑的改动文件树（支持一键收起释放全宽画布）。想看某处具体改了哪几行代码时，点一下「核心必看」文件胶囊或右侧文件树，右侧立即滑出修改前后代码对照抽屉，主页面原地不动、不乱滚。 ## 安装与使用 ### 安装 **方式一 · 命令行安装** ```bash npx skills add oil-oil/oil-diff ``` **方式二 · 直接发给 Agent 安装** ```text 请帮我安装这个 Skill： ``` ### 日常使用 安装后，直接在对话里告诉 Agent 你想看哪部分改动即可： ```text 用 oil-diff 把当前分支最近的改动做成汇报页。 ``` ```text 用 oil-diff 整理目前还没提交的修改，生成一份 HTML 改动汇报。 ``` ```text 用 oil-diff 对比 main..HEAD 的改动，看看这轮到底改了哪几件事。 ``` ## 适用边界、数据与运行环境 - **零污染仓库状态**：生成的网页与数据全部放在 ` /.oil-diff/` 目录下，并自动对 Git 隐形，不修改项目原本的任何文件，也不影响 `git status`。 - **单文件离线可用**：最终生成的 `.oil-diff/index.html` 是零外部依赖的单文件网页，双击就能在浏览器打开，也可以直接发给同事查看。 - **配置与兼容性**：无需额外配置 API Key 或环境变量；仅依赖系统 `git` 与 Python 3.10+ 标准库，支持 macOS、Windows 与 Linux。 ## 许可证 MIT License
